question:
What is the value of

\[ \begin{gathered} 2(81 + 83 + 85 + 87 + 89 \\ {}+ 91 + 93 + 95 + 97 + 99)? \end{gathered} \]
solution:
Pair the smallest term with the largest, then work inward. The pairs are
\[
81+99,\quad83+97,\quad85+95,
\]
\[
87+93,\quad89+91.
\]
Each pair totals \(180\), and the five pairs use all ten terms exactly once. Thus the sum inside the parentheses is \(5\cdot180=900\). Including the outside factor gives
\[
2\cdot900=\boxed{1800},
\]
choice E.

edges.reason: Written addition prepares vertical alignment and repeated carrying. In multiplication the carried amount is added to one digit product, so the full three-digit column-addition procedure is not executed.

The general digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm contains digit products with seven, eight and nine. Their values are required, without demanding rote recitation as the exclusive way to obtain them.

Two-digit division broadens which expression steps can be computed. The precedence convention and a three-step calculation can also be practiced with one-digit divisors; the wider algorithm is preparation.
Longer column sums motivate efficient regrouping. Commutativity and associativity can be understood and used on small or round-number mental sums without the written three-digit procedure.
edges.scope: verifying and applying addition laws on larger numbers
